headline: Agima reports a single omni model planning with imagined visual outcomes in four simulated tasks
summary: An Oct. 19 preprint introduces Agima, which trains one 14B-parameter omni model (7B active) to propose actions, generate visual predictions of their outcomes, and plan from those imagined observations before acting. The authors report results across Maze2D, Sokoban, Pacman and PushT. In a four-box Sokoban test with real feedback every five actions, the SFT model solves 40% of puzzles versus 2% for an action-only model fine-tuned from the same backbone. Replacing imagined observations with blank or stale frames sharply reduces success; oracle observations improve it, linking the reported gains to prediction content. Results are author-reported in simulated tasks; the research desk did not reproduce them, and the paper reports no inference FLOPs or latency.
